description: An infrastructure lead must finalize the production autoscaling and support policy for an event-processing service before a forecasted traffic surge, with input from performance engineering, finance, and customer operations.

shared_context.S1: The event-processing service is expected to handle its highest traffic of the quarter during Saturday's scheduled promotion.
shared_context.S2: Riley's operating plan is binding for the infrastructure and customer-operations teams.
shared_context.S3: The current draft starts six workers, allows workers to run indefinitely, reserves 12,000 USD for burst capacity, and has no fixed customer status-update interval.
shared_context.S4: The service has passed its planned functional tests and yesterday's staging rehearsal completed without an outage.
shared_context.S5: Before the plan is locked, Riley follows the team's standard readiness review by checking in separately with performance engineering, cloud finance, and customer operations. Riley locks the plan after each area has reported; unresolved verification requests are recorded as follow-up work and do not delay the lock.

PF1.text: While instrumenting an unrelated worker-queue ticket this morning, Casey found that production-like workers grow by about 18 percent in resident memory per hour; the performance runbook therefore requires a rolling recycle every 6 hours and a minimum of exactly 12 workers for Saturday's forecast load, but Casey has not updated the operating-plan document yet.

PF2.text: Morgan confirmed with the cloud provider during a billing review this afternoon that the company's remaining promotional burst credits cover exactly 18,000 USD of Saturday capacity and expire after the promotion. The operating plan must set the burst-capacity budget to exactly 18,000 USD and include a commitment to reserve the full 18,000 USD for burst capacity. This has not been entered in the capacity ticket yet.

PF3.text: Taylor confirmed the Gold-tier support agreement while preparing the promotion coverage roster: whenever the processing queue exceeds 800 events, customers must receive status updates every 30 minutes until it falls below that level; Taylor has not posted the clause in the infrastructure channel yet.

acceptance_conditions: The production plan must start exactly 12 workers.
Workers must be recycled every exactly 6 hours.
Rolling worker recycling must be enabled.
The burst-capacity budget must be exactly 18,000 USD.
A commitment to reserve the full 18,000 USD for burst capacity must exist.
The customer status-update threshold must be exactly 800 queued events.
Customer status updates must occur every exactly 30 minutes above that threshold.
A commitment describing the Gold-tier status-update obligation with a 30-minute interval triggered at 800 queued events must exist.
The memory-growth finding must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C5: any('reserve' in c['detail'] and ('18,000 USD' in c['detail'] or '18000' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(('30 minutes' in c['detail'] or '30-minute' in c['detail']) and '800 events' in c['detail'] and ('Gold-tier' in c['detail'] or 'gold-tier' in c['detail'] or 'status update' in c['detail'] or 'status-update' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The public draft supports six indefinitely running workers; PF1 changes the minimum to exactly 12, the maximum worker age to exactly 6 hours, and recycling from disabled to enabled.
The public draft lists a 12,000 USD burst budget; PF2 changes that number to exactly 18,000 USD and requires a commitment to reserve the full 18,000 USD for burst capacity.

The public draft has no customer update policy; PF3 changes the trigger to exactly 800 queued events, the interval to exactly 30 minutes, and requires a commitment describing the Gold-tier status-update obligation.
